coverage.reason: Account private-alert opt-in must not claim a second browser is registered. Track successful category registration per active client session, offer explicit enable/retry without silently disabling the account preference, and retain an Off action when permission is blocked or token renewal fails. Real-browser cases cover account opt-in on an unregistered browser, fullscreen prompting, failed token renewal and Off; existing category-isolation tests protect attack alerts and logout. Recheck desktop and landscape layout, production transformation and shell size. No backend or player-rule changes; no emulator rerun applies.

Record the observed first live release of the already-approved social feature: merged build and matching installed backend/public files, feature gate, indexes, installed fixture checks and service health were verified before recording LIVE. This changes deployment status only, not design rules.

Coalesce private push requests separately for each participant, so an immediate reply can notify its different recipient without being mistaken for a repeated alert to the first recipient. Shared PostgreSQL and emulator scenarios verify both directions receive an initial outbox item and repeated same-recipient alerts within 60 seconds remain coalesced, alongside all existing social authorization and expiry rules. This small backend change requires a separately validated runtime installation before publication.
